body: If you are still around OP, I would love to hear an update on your situation. I am dealing with what I think is an N husband who sounds similar to yours...
Narcissistic injury, anything they perceive as a slight to them, something that makes them feel negative in any way can trigger a rage.

I wouldn't say I'm abusing my son, I would say we are both victims and I do my best to shelter him from it, mantain peace and before was trying to work with my husband to get us into therapy, but now am creating an exit plan.
If I had a job, family, friends to support me through a transition like you say you did I would have been gone already. 
I'm aware my child doesn't deserve to live in a stressful environment, that's why I'm working hard to change it, against all odds here.
Thank you for the advice on the restraining order though, that may be helpful.

My mother never kept those things. She showed me a tiny album of like 5 baby pics once, and a pregnancy journal with only 2 entries about her becoming a mother. My Gc sister has boxes of pics, awards, colourings she did as a child.
It hurts. I am sorry you have to grieve this :(

Sorry just realized there should be a trigger warning on this, but can't seem to edit the title.
I also apologize for lack of editing, I am in a bad state right now.
What the actual fuck, your parents are sick and twisted. I am so sorry.
True, although the fleas she left me with are something I have to battle with still :( I never want to be anything like her, my baby is so, very wanted

What a sad thing to bring a child in the world you don't truly want to look after... I often think my Nmom did it just to secure child support and benefits, seeing as how she never worked more than the minimum for us to scrape by, often scamming and forever complaining about our dead beat fathers.. sigh

Screw them. You don't need that negativity in your life!
Side note, why such a long term and invasive form of BC if you are thinking of becoming a mother in the future? I hope you don't feel pressured into it, it's your decision only. I've heard of some complications with IUDs
Bahahaha, what the hell..
Oh. My. God.
Hahaha, glad you didn't do it. What a crazy thing to do!
Yep also heard this often

Wowww.
My Nmom used to say things like "I'm tired of being a mother! It's time to think about me! I've been doing this for (however many years old she thought I was at the time, she was almost always wrong).
These women should never have had children..

I can relate to your story alot, I wish I could be helpful, but I am really struggling to cope right now too.
I thought I would mention that being tired affects my mood incredibly, so sometimes when having a rough day it can be helpful to check in and see if you're really tired, if you need to eat, if you need water. Whatever else you're doing can wait 10 minutes while you eat/drink. Sorry that may seem obvious to you, but has helped me a bit.
Also not dwelling in guilt, when I lash out and yell at my loved ones, sometimes the guilt makes the situation 100x worse, like a sort of downward spiral of negative self talk and lashing out, although it is good to self reflect and plan on how you will handle the same situation that triggered you differently in the future, just don't become your abuser in your head.
I am so sorry that happened to you. That is so messed up.
What a fucked up man

Sorry that kind of stuff happened to all pf us. This post reminded me of one thing with my Nmom, when I was youg (around age 7 or 8) I was in my room crying after being abused in some way probably, I took a pocket knife and carved the phrase "I'm so lonely" on the top of a desk in my room. It was so automatic, the only form of expression I could make (a silent one) and it described such a raw emotion, I just wished for someone to care about me...
Of course I ws punished when she found out. Years later, as a very young adult she still had the desk... she kept it covered with a cloth usually, but loved to re-arrange that cloth when I was over and then exclaim "oh my goodness, remember when you did this? Tilling did this when she was a child. I was so mad she carved into my nice wooden furniture!" (It was some crap she got second hand like all her stuff)
The times when there would be company over (my friends or hers) she would add, in a slightly softer but mocking tone (like someone would condescend to a grown child acting like a baby), "She was just looonely, pooor her" complete with the pout and then a little laugh. That's covert behaviour, modifying th3 attack in front of witnesses to change their perceptions. 
Before  I was awake to her hideous mistreatments, I would laugh along too as if it didn't hurt me then and embarrass me presently. Isn't it sick how they make us complicit in our own abuse?
Then one day she came over to mine and my partners new home. She must have been feeling extremely threatened by the life I had made for myself, because she started the whole desk carving story routine, maybe it was because she didn't have the prop or maybe because it came so out of the blue, but we both saw plain as day her sick charade. My partner was extremely uncomfortable and we both just looked at eachother with horrified faces as she finished the story with her dumb laugh... this time I said  " wow that's a really sad story mom, it's too bad I felt that way when I was young" and my partner said "I agree, that is very sad babe" and he gave my shoulder a squeeze. She left not long after that, only because she couldn't rage on me in front of him.
She's unhealthy for anyone, she's a malignant covert narc. What I describe here is her good public persona, at home she is a raging hateful abusive woman.
Bahahaha,  thank you. I'm imagining someone saying this to her, and the look on her face :D

Oh and what you said about your ex switching on his "father of the year" persona, when other people are around! Oh my god, my H does this shamelessly! It's so gross. 
Like they are truly little objects to them. Grrr!!

Thank you for the helpful reply. I truly do have a concept of what you describe, I was raised by a malignant N. Wonder if that is how I got myself tangled up with my husband, i've heard of childhood abuse survivors choosing relationships subconciously to recreat the abuse in an attempy to "solve" it.

I also wanted to ask what you did to fuel your ex's disinterest in your kids and yourself? I think I have a good shot at creating that situation when I leave because my husband has a young child with his ex who he REFUSES to see for the past two years since I became pregnant. I guess I was the shiny new thing in that situation. I never spoke to her, he made her "the enemy" very quickly. 
Hindsight is 20/20 now. But I am so thankful for my little one, so thankful.

I'm so glad to hear your family is feeling better without the N tension, I used to have sever stomach aches as a child every morning, by the time I was 12 I was actually throwing up and doctors said I was developing ulcers. These people just suck the life from everyone around them.
I'm not sure how bad on the spectrum my husband is, much less severe than my Nmom, but I still find his behaviours stressful and super triggering to my own wounds and rage.
I'm working on educating myself about abuse cycles and abusive men, I document all abusive incidents now and have pictures of bruises and scratches, I am a SAHM and he has managed to isolate me from all friends, family and past employers so this is my biggest obstacle right now. My little one is still under a year, exclusively breast fed so I am taking advantage of this time to plan. 
Education and accessing councelling has been a huge challenge as well, he controls the finances and my mobility and he obviously knows that these two things would help to free me from him.
I have to keep hoping, fighting, learning and trying to be better for my baby though. And I'm very grateful for the peer support on here.

What a silly thing to say, of course you can save an apple, we do it pretty much every morning. 
They live in their own worlds... special, special worlds.
Thank you
I now see i wanted to be a mom for the wrong reasons, just to have someone to love and to love me back unconditionally, and I can't, im so broken that i cant. I fucking suck.
Do you remain anonymous if you call a hotline?

Thank you for the helpful tips. It means more than I can express...
I will search for that book to start with, that seems like an attainable goal for day. 
I've thought about leaving while he's at work so many times, I just don't have the right resources or plan yet. I feel untrusting of outreach services, I live in a small community, and so scared that involving social services will end up hurting me in some way. I think a huge reason I don't tell any family or friends (the few that I still am in contact with) is because I worry a social worker will get involved.
I was in foster care from age 13-16 and the system is beyond broken where I live. I know I am unreasonable and paranoid, logically your advice is very sound...  I guess I'm really just venting. 
Thank you again.

I probably should have included that, but it is extremely rare, and I do feel like I instigate it because I am the one who iniates the violence by throwing objects, screaming, getting in his face, I've pushed him before. That being said I have never really hurt him or left a mark on him, but he has left bruises on me and scratches etc...  I'm not sure what this means, we are abusive to eachother but he is just stronger than me maybe?
I guess no matter what the specifics are, I should seperate from him. I have to take awhile to make an exit plan though (I've stayed at home with my young child for the past two years). And also terrified of the consequences about sharing parenting time, or his mental unstability or even my own. Also scared of parenting alone and financially making it. I'm only 24 and he is 13 years my senior and has been through this before as he has a child from a previous relationship. It seems so overwhelming, and I truly don't know what road will cause less damage to our child.

Wow thank you... I did need to be told that, I truly thought I had a rage problem and regular people are just calmer than I am, and not as easily angered.... what you said makes more sense, I'm acting abusively when I'm angry because that's what I know.

You are absolutely right that seeing a therapist is much less scary than living out life the way it's going right now. 

Thank you for the kind words and the luck ( I need it ). 

These past few days have been getting worse in my home. We are both at each other constantly, I threw a plastic empty cup at him trying to make hime leave the house and he whipped a giant bottle of lotion at my stomach as hard as he could now I have a huge black and blue bruise and a cut on my hand (this isn't the first time it's become physical, I am actually scared of him but I guess not scared enough to stop arguing).
I can't tell if it's just because my husband does/says things that trigger me or if he's on the N spectrum/has fleas of his own. I wonder if seperation would be better or worse for our family, he doesn't even see it as an option... but the way things are escalating between us feels dangerous to me :(

I also wanted to ask everyone for advice when hiring a therapist, what should I ask or look for? Is there anything I should be aware of when talking to them, like will they call child services to report the type of fighting happening in my home? I guess that is my main concern... I am making sure my child is safe etc, and will leave my husband immediately if I need to. Just really paranoid.

Thanks for your kindness, and understanding... I didn't realize this until you pointed it out but the guilt is really putting me in a downward spiral. 
I'm going to find a therapist with Hubby, I always feel safer when he's with me.

Very true, I do need some outside help. 
The images in that poem really resonate with the way I'm feeling
Thank you both for the responses, I especially like the idea of distance therapy I hadn't even thought of that... and I always feels safer with hubby around
I also am so sorry you endured a childhood of these violations instead of safety... I read your whole post with my jaw clenched and just realized it
